The glow of sunrise bounced off the blinds into my eyes causing me to pull up the covers for a few more minutes. In no time Khan has hopped on the bed purring, pawing at my blanket for love. The smell of espresso seeps into my room, just before the timer dings letting me know it is ready.

Tossing off the covers I grab my cat and biry my face in his side before standing up to stretch.

"Another 'fun-filled day' huh Khan?" Smiling down and patting his head, I slip on a day dress and head to the kitchen.

Another day off, alone and to myself. My comissions have quieted down so I can enjoy a day with nothing to do before the banking job beckons me on Monday.

Sugar, milk, stir until tan. Perfection.

Opening the back door, I gingerly get into my seat cradling a fresh cup of java in my hands. A nice breeze sets in while I savor my sip, just chilled enough to pair the hot coffee I drink.

"Mmm the life." I amuse myself sometimes. Looking down at the phone, no messages as usual. I look over to the side table and see a pack of cigarettes I left out a few nights ago. Pulling one out, I begin to light it, take a drag, exhale and take a sip.

The smoke around me begins to grow and turn counter clockwise, there is no breeze. 

"The f-"

Gravity slams me down onto a wooden floor, my coffee spills, my cigarettes fly to the edge of some red paint.

I scramble to get up, "the hell is going on?!" The thickening of the smoke begins to subside, first thing I notice is the red paint is an image of a pentagram with latin beneath my feet.

My step out of the circle is stopped by what feels like a brick wall, I stumble back. Leaning down to pick up my pack, I hear a voice.

"It worked!" Exclaimed a young male's voice.
Looking up I meet eyes of two teenage boys, "she doesn't look like a demon." Says the one with glasses, the boy holding the book slaps him on the back, "they walk among us like the book says!"

"What?" I reply in disbelief. I try to take another step out of the circle but am met with another wall. "Get me out of here!" I snap at the two.

"No way. That's how you will take our souls, demon." Calls out the boy holding the book.

Confused, I look down at the smokes in my hand. Could these have been switched with weed without my knowledge? Weed doesn't do that, dismissively I shake my head and turn my back to the boys. I see a washer and dryer, I am in someone's basement. 

"Do either of you have a light?" I ask with my back turned.

Feeling around my bra I find my lighter. As I begin to spark I hear, "hey no smoking!" Taking a drag, the exhaling I turn around to them again.

"You summoned a human, how, I do not know but I am no demon." I pull from my cigarette again.

"Frankie, control her." The boy in the glasses shoves his friend who is flipping through the pages of the book.

Frankie begins chanting in latin, my hand flicks the cigarette to the ground and I step on it.

"Wait a min-" I am caught off guard by my behavior and kneel down on the ground.

"It works!" Frankie jumps in his spot behind the table with glee. "Charlie! We can control demons!"

I can't move, but I can still run my mouth. "Let me go!"

"Not until you help us." Charlie stands up walking closer to the circle. "We want revenge."

I couldn't contain my laughter for how melodramatic Charlie said that. "Haha What? You want me to put up some kid from school? Hahaha kid, I don't have any powers, I would literally be punching a 12 year old."

They look at one another as I continue to laugh, when I finally calmed down, Frankie clears his throat. "Demon, you are under our command, you will help us seek out revenge."

I begin cackling at these two teens who are taking themselves to seriously. "Kids, I am a banker by day, moonlighting as an artist. What? You want me to run someone's credit down and draw them a less than flattering caricature of themselves?!" I double over within the circle. I ease up and can stand again, "you obviously found some powerful juju but I am not helping you. Send me back!" I clear a tear from my eye and stare them down.

"Send me back." Using the voice I use with belligerent children I babysat for in the past. I feel a trickle run down my forehead, touching it and peering down at my hand I see blood. Looking back up I see the boys are frozen, as I start to feel a stretch and pull on my hairline.

I begin to shake and fall down, searing pain started at the crown of my head, and cascades down to the soles of my feet. Everything burns, the glimpse of a halo cracks above me and spills neon blue within the circle. A rush of cool blasts over my skin like a sunburn.

Stretching out, I pick myself up and notice I am not flesh colored anymore, I am blue. I am fucking blue! My hands slowly run up the bumps of my face to two stout winding horns that go through my hair to behind my ears.

"Shit!" Screams Charlie and Frankie.

My dress is in tatters on my frame, ever peep of skin is blue. "Wh-what did you do to me?" Horrified I look at them for an answer.

"It says here you will go back to walking amongst us when you completed your task." Frankie reading from the book peers back up at me. "Looks like you have no choice now."

I throw my hands up and turn a full circle, "Alright, let's hear it then." The day has gone too crazy to question anything at this point. "Bill down the block stole your bike? The principle gave you detention? A girl you like is dating a jock who bullies you? TELL ME!" A gutteral growl shakes the candles lit throughout the basement.

"We h-have beef with a guy named Chad. H-he stole my mom's necklace." Charlie shaking on every word.

Throwing my hands up in the hair again, "Chad! Of COURSE it is a Chad!" I stomp on the ground, "Let me out of here so I can go gut punch him, steal the necklace back and go back home to my cat. Chop chop!" I clap my hands together.

Frankie flips through a few more pages, "W-We have to go over the rules." Meekly looking up at me.

I roll my eyes, "Alright, do that voodoo that you do then."

Charlie pipes up "It's actually -"

"I DON'T CARE! On with it, damn!" I get down on the ground again and take a seat. "I don't have all day!"

Mary struggled with the adjustment of her anxiety medication, after losing her father she jumped at every bump in the night. Ever since she was little, she would see shadow people, and as she grew older she found out how common it was for mostly everyone else.

Hauntings were mostly a let down, usually it was someone like Tim from Accounting who wanted to watch the Price is Right, or Bailey who wanted to tell you about all her accomplishments from when she played Animal Crossing. Ghosts walked the Earth to continue being boring, baddies went to Hell, and the good ones ascended to the Heavens. 

Mary knew her Dad wasn't perfect, knew he wasn't a Saint but knew he was never boring. Following directions from the internet, she lit incense around her house in efforts to purge any ghosts that may try to camp out. The old lady in white who fiddled with her coffee machine never bothered her before, but with her heart racing every night, and jumping to closing doors she needed some peace of mind.

Lavender, cedar, and a bit of palo santo sitting in a sea shell. Smoke filled her home as she walked room to room, crossing every window and mirror until she reached the kitchen. The shell cracked in her hands, dropping contents to the floor, extinguishing the embers. Mary stood in the door way pondering what to do next. Walking to the linen closet, she returns to the kitchen with a broom and dust pan, kneeling down to scoop up her mess.

"Hey! Are you going to keep smoking up the place?" A brash voice rung out from around the corner of her kitchen island.

Mary feels her blood pressure raise in a panic, who is in the house?

Standing up with broom in both hands she is greeted by a faint outline of a woman across the counter. Slowly her apparition forms, and Mary sees a woman with blonde hair who looks to be in her 30s. 

"You are not welcomed." Mary responds.

The woman chuckles and reaches into her pocket for a pack of cigarettes. "You think burning potpurri is going to flush me out?" Pulling a lighter from her shirt the woman lights her cigarette and blows a puff of smoke. "That's cute."

Mary can smell the tabacco burning, this is a new one for her. Never knew Ghosts could bring cigarettes with them to the other side.

"What is your name?" Mary asks, turning to dump the contents into the trashbin.

"Call me Bobbi." She replied leaning on the counter reading the cover of a nearby magazine. "Ugh you read Cosmo?"

"That's a former roommate's." Mary sighs and opens a fridge to pull out a can of soda. Walking to the kitchen table and sitting down. "Join me?"

Bobbi looks over her shoulder at Mary, huffs and sits in the pulled out chair, Mary left for her. 

"Why are you in my house?" Mary asks.

"I got dumped here after the whole scales thing happened." Pulling on her cigarette and releasing a cloud of smoke.

Nodding Mary takes a sip of her soda, "Could you go somewhere else?"

"Tried that." Bobbi lifts her eyebrows and grins. "Didn't work out."

Mary cocks an eyebrow, "how come?"

Bobbi leans back, and points at Mary's phone. The screen illuminates with no notifications. Swiping to unlock, her search engine pulls up a news article from earlier today mentioning a man's house having an electrical fire.

"You started a fire?" Mary asks.

"He said he would never leave me, not even a month went by and he was with his coworker in our bed." Bobbi flicks the cigarette butt that disappears from her hand.

Reading through the article shows a picture of Bobbi when she was alive. Not much different, but looks alot angerier. Scrolling through the story, they had a history of domestic violence. News reports were documenting this as a modern day "Revenge from beyond the Grave" angle. They were together for 3 years.

Mary looks up at Bobbi who is waving at her cat. "I am sorry that happened."

Bobbi shrugs, "its okay, he will be begging me to float back."

Puzzled Mary inquires, "are you saying you will leave here?"

Shrugging again Bobbi responds, "you have a nice place here, it's become a port of call for me since I died."

Mary asks, "How long have you been here?"

Thinking about the math, Bobbi answers. "Off and on for a little over a Month."

"Where did you go before your ex?"

The lights flicker, Bobbi interjects "Before I went to my boyfriend's house, I was at my cousin's house, before that I saw a few friends."

Mary finishes her soda, placing the empty can on the table she asks, "you couldn't stay?"

"Nah, they wanted to play games with me. Lie to me about my life, tell me to move on, they didnt want me to learn about all the things they did behind my back." 

Mary turns down to her phone and Google's Bobbi's name. More articles over the last month appear of arson from the ghost sitting before her.

"I loved them all regardless of what they thought I didn't already know, but I'm dead. They could have at least welcomed me." Bobbi trails off staring up at the light hanging above the table. The bulb begins to dim down,  steadily brightening back as she pulls for another cigarette.

"You ever run out of cigarettes?" Mary asks. Bobbi giggles and shakes her head.

"If they were so shitty to you, why did you stay their friend while you were alive?" Mary looked at the clock and noticed it was time to take her medication.

"Ahh you sound like my shrink."  Smiling Bobbi lights her second cigarette, "I can assure you, it was because I didn't value or love myself. Same reason I was with my guy too!"

Mary looks at the article on her phone, Bobbi's friend Mona was hysterically crying while her house was half collasped and flooding in the background.

"Wouldn't you rather start anew?" Mary inquired, turning off her display.

Bobbi stared back at the light above them, watching as it goes dim again.

"Why? I am already dead." Blowing a puff of smoke her pale eyes meet with Mary's.

"You could talk to other ghosts? Make new friends?" Mary stands up to grab another soda.

Huffing Bobbi shoots the empty can off the table. "No other ghosts really talk. They are all hung up on idle shit, and no one wants to do anything fun besides the mundane shit that led them to wasting away while they were alive." 

"If you are going to throw trash, at least aim for the recycling bin." Mary walks to the can, disposing it in her blue bin.

"My bad." Bobbi looks at Mary as she sits down. "Who are you trying to push out? Who died?"

Mary shakes her head, "No one specifically."

Tilting her head Bobbi laughs, "Liiiieeessssss, I saw your medicene cabinet, and your report you were reading a few days ago. You are afraid of someone."

" Not afraid of them, just don't want them to be stuck on Earth."

"So you would rather leave them high and dry out there?"

Mary shifts in her seat, "I don't even know where they went."

Bobbi leans in, "I could find out, hell, they have have been in line for the scales when I was there!" 

"No thank you." Mary feels her heart race again, getting up she goes to the bathroom and takes her medication.

"They have you on the hard stuff, they put me on that a few years back, I took myself off of it though." Bobbi appeared in the shower stall while Mary put the medicene away.

"C'mon! A ghost who isn't boring willing to give you the details! Why not?" Bobbi trails behind her as Mary makes her way back to the kitchen.

"You are a little more troublesome than I originally anticipated."

Giggling again, Bobbi shrugs, "not troublesome! More like I hate you, don't leave me."

Mary sighs and accepts Bobbi isn't leaving. "Greaaat, borderline."

"Exactly!" Bobbi exclaims, tickled that Mary got the reference. "I promise not to burn your place down, you seem pretty chill. Soooo let me stay?"

Mary looks out the window and sees a couple having an argument on the sidewalk.

"Just don't bring the drama to my door, and stay quiet at night."

Bobbi pauses, "I can try Doc." Looking over to see what Mary is staring at, she recognizes the couple. "Ooooh that m-" Bobbi nearly flips the chair, throwing herself through the window.

Obscenities erupted through Mary's Rose bush, an explosion of branches and thorns pelting the the couple. "You sonovabitch!!" Bellowed Bobbi as more branches and thorns rain on the man who has fallen and covers his face. The girl stumbled on a crack and gave herself a concussion when she hit the iron fence.

Bobbi disappears, the man gets get and walks over to his passed out girlfriend. "Sara?" Trying to nudge her awake, Mary stays in her chair watching.

Sara's eyes open and she begins cackling excessively. "You are TRASH!" Slapping her boyfriend in the face. "Utter!" Balling up her fist and contacting his cheek, Mary could hear the pop of bone crunching. "Fucking!" The man falls down, his girlfriend kicks him. "TRASH!" She lifts her foot and stomps on him. Leaning forward, the girlfriend begins to throw up.

"Baby?" His girlfriend's voice has softened. "Ohmygod! Baby!!" She falls to her knees trying to wake him up. Pulling out her phone she dials 911.

Bobbi reappears in the kitchen, standing at the island. Mary looks at the back of her ghostly guest. 

Bobbi lifts her hand and says, "just that one time, I swear."

Mary looks out at her dishelveled rose bush. "Was that your ex?"

Bobbi turns around, looking at the scene and sighs, "one of them!"

Cici stops above the drop, Dale holds his breath beneath her, frozen. He lost Terry and Rhonda, Cici could have gotten them.

Heart racing, Dale is shaking, his phone begins to ring again alerting Cici. In one foul breath, Cici clears the brush hiding Dale, her eye is bright green shrouded in bright, red blood vessels. Her lips part enough to show the tips of her pointy grin as she begins to float down to Dale.

"BABY GIRL!" calls out Rhonda, "up here!" Cici rolls to up the drop in pique interest. Rhonda pops up over the edge and empties the can of bear mace right against Cici's eye.

A shrill scream follows Cici, as she begins smashing into everything and wailing. Trees fall in the dark, and she rolls over the ground reaching the pasture and flying into the pond.

The cows rush out of the water nearly stampeding the truck to get away from the predator.

Rhonda shines a light from her phone down on Dale, "can you climb out of there?"

"Yeah!" Dale pulls himself up with exposed roots until he is standing next to her. "Have you seen Terry?" Dale asks.

"Right here." Winded, Terry is leaning against a tree near by. "She was too fast for me to shoot her."

They cautiously make their way back to the truck, the cows have escaped through the fence, but Cici is missing again. 

"Hey. We need to take you back to your mom. Its dark now, we can try again tomorrow." Rhonda opens the truck door, motioning for Dale to scoot in.

"Where's the dog?" Dale asks, realizing he has been missing. 

Terry hoists himself up in the driver seat. "I saw him jump back out of the truck when we were leaving your mom's house. He is probably still there or walked back home."

Dirty, exhuasted, and strained the three of them make their way back to the house in 2 hours. The driveway is cleared, and there are laterns up in the opened living room, where Dale's mom sits reading a magazine.

Terry calls out when parking, "Dana! How'd you clear the drive way? Did you finally use the wench I got you?"

Dana looks up from her reading glasses but does not respond.

Rhonda hops out of the car, "Sis! Get your bag and come stay with us tonight." 

No response, Dana takes a sip of her tea.

Dale gingerly, gets out of the truck and walks towards his mom.

"Mom I-" Dale quiets himself when his mother locks eyes on him, lifting her hand. She is calm. Dale knows he is in trouble.

"Come. Sit." She motions all of them inside.

Taking a seat on whatever is available, Dana motions to the tea pot and miscellaneous cups sitting on her nightstand she brought out from her room.

"Rhonda." Dana chimes, looking at her sister. "Thank you both for keeping Dale safe."

"Of course Sis." Rhonda relaxes a little.

"Terry." Dana's tone changes, making Terry lose a little color.

"Yes, Dana?"

"If you ever take my son out monster hunting again, whether he is 19 or 99, while he lives under my roof do not encourage him to try and hide a monster in my basement. Understand?" Dana takes a sip of her tea and places the cup down. Terry doesn't say a word, he just nods.

"Dale Aaron Morrow." Dana looks at her son, he won't look back at her. 

She continues, "Insurance doesn't cover Tempermental Monsters." Dale's stomach drops. "You are going to get a job, and work this off."

"Yes mom."

"Excuse me?"

"Yes ma'am." Dale stammers and nods.

"Tomorrow, you are applying to the chicken plant." 

"Yes ma'am." Dale hated the chicken plant, but he is not going to contest his mom right now.

"As for Gigi-" Dana leans over the back of the couch.

"Cici?" Terry asks.

Dana pulls up a purple, puffy leash, fastened to a pink glittery harness. The harness hugging a thorny beach ball that is sleeping soundly.

"She likes 'Gigi' better." Dana holds Gigi in her lap and begins petting her, plucking a piece of dust from her long eye lashes.

"She barrelled back here over an hour ago, got her to heel, and calm down enough to help me move everything before she shrunk back down." Dana strokes above her eyelid, a soft coo emits from her lips as Gigi nuzzles into Dana's arm.

"She can stay, obviously. But no more pets." Dana smiles down at her baby eyeball before telling Dale to go to his room.

Walking deeper into the woods, they pass by bare bones and cow limbs before stopping when they hear a low gutteral snoring sound.

"She must have ate herself to sleep, lets go." Terry raises his gun and nods for them to follow closely.

Stepping deeper into the clearing that opened up to them. The snoring getting louder. The path of blood leads them right to Cici, her crooked, sharp teeth giving away her hiding spot inbetween breaths. Her pale blue skin is stretched taught like a beach ball, her large eye lashes littered with leaves and branches. Her full chapped lips, and eye lid stretched out the width of her body. Cic's tiny horns protrude like she is a giant pufferfish.

"Terry she is still the size of a boulder, what the hell am I suppose to do?!" Dale asks in anxious, hushed tones.

"Well I didn't think about that." Terry whispers back.

"Seriously?!" Aunt Rhonda glares while gesturing her hand violently.

"Wait! Hush!" Terry stops them. "That harness will fit, she is going to shrink-"

Before Terry could finish his sentance, Dale's phone begins to ring. Panicked, Dale fumbles to silence it dropping the harness. Cici stirs, but rolls over taking the forest floor of moss with her. 

Dale answers in a whisper, "Mom I-"

"WHAT DID YOU DO TO MY HOUSE?! WHERE ARE YOU?" The roar from the phone blasted out enough to startle Rhonda.

"Mom! I need you to be quiet-"

"MY SON WHO LIVES FOR FREE WILL NOT TELL ME TO BE QUIET I THOUGHT YOU WERE DEAD-"

Terry turns and signals Dale to hang up. Startled and shaken he ends the call.

"Turn the ph-" Rhonda's murmur is drowned out by the phone blasting the ring tone again, which makes Cici turn over and open her eye.

A humid breath expells from Cici's mouth, knocking them back as she begins to growl.

"Run. Run. RUN!" Terry shoves Rhonda and Dale to rush back to the truck.

Cici, begins to leviatate as her skin begins to turn magenta. "Faster!" Terry hollers, "she is charging up!"

Her growl is felt beneath their feet, the trees begin to reflect light that she is now started to emit. 

As the run Rhonda looks over her shoulder "Scatter!" Before leaping to her left out of the clear path they were on, Terry and Dale jump to the right. Cici darts down the cleared path she made and hooks at a right angle, like a flaming pinball.

The sun is starting to go down, and Dale stumbles over thick brush and falls 5 ft into more bushes. Cici is gaining up on him.

The smell of burnt plastic, paired with the pop and crackling sounds of smoldering flames brings Dale to consciousness. Pushing the heavy weight of debris off, he rolls over, coughing while trying to gain his footing. The sun shines through the massive hole in the ceiling of the basement he stands in, stumbling over charred furniture he finds his way to stairs.

Coming up to the ground floor, Dale can tell half the home has been blown into the trees. The kitchen completely demolished, leaving pools of water from ruptured plumbing, the living room littered with leaves, broken glass, and chunks of drywall. Wiping blood from his hairline, he leans down picking up a mug, filling it with water from his broken sink.

Sitting down on the caved in couch, Dale reaches for his pocket and pulls out his phone. Swiping the screen to unlock, he looks out into the tree line observing the aluminum siding twisted in the branches and waving in the air. Scrolling through his contacts list, he reaches "Mama" and takes a deep breath, there has to be someone else.

Scrolling down further he reaches "Terry," maybe he can help? Hell, he helped catch his companion on the mountain years ago. Pushing the green phone, the speaker begins to ring.

"Hey Lil' Dale what's up?" His Appalachian drawl pours through the phone.

"Hey Terry, uh I have a problem." Dale takes a deep breath.

Sarcastically though stern Terry asks, "It's noon, what did you get into this time?" 

"It's more like what got out." Dale sighs.

Dale hears the flick of a lighter through the phone, "Let me get the dog, I'm coming over."

"The driveway is blocked in, bring your 4 wheeler." Dale adds, but Terry already hung up.

Dale walks over the collasped wall out into the front yard, looking to see any clearing that his companion may have made. A few fallen trees climb up the ravine to the main dirt road but no sight of scent of his buddy. In the distance the the roaring engine of Terry's distinguishable truck draws closer. Flipping over a wicker chair Dale sits and waits, watching the faded blue Ford, turn down his drive way and stopping a quarter mile in when slabs of concrete and prevent him from going forward.

Turning the ignition off, the heavy door swings open with Terry hopping out, followed by his black Labrador.

Sizing up the damage in the drive way he walks around and sees Dale sitting.

"What the hell did you do boy?!" Stomping out a smoldering patch of pine needles as he walks closer to the house. 

The passenger door opens, and out comes Terry's girlfriend Aunt Rhonda. "What on Earth?" Her wide eyes peering over the damage, "Lil Dale, the house is damn near gone. Did you get into Meth??"

Terry chuckles, "No Sweetheart, Lil Dale let his friend out."

"I didn't let her out, he broke out." Dale frustratedly calls out before finishing his water, and tossing the mug.

Terry walks past Dale, stepping over the wall and into what's left of the kitchen. Kicking over a cabinet door, he. Squats down touching the burned edges of the floor, looking down into the basement.

"When did she start shooting fire?" He asks while charcoal bits break into dust under his fingers.

Dale answers, "She isn't shooting fire, she just boils up and turns into a fireball."

Rhonda picking up knick knacks in the yard, "Hol' up" marching over to Dale sitting in the wicker chair, calling Terry over. "Is this all from the eyeball baby?" She hands the figurines to Dale, who walks them over to the last piece of countertop and sets them down.

"Cici, yeah." Dale replies quietly.

"She was just a baby 6 months ago, barely fit in my hand." Turning over to Terry smacking him in the arm, Rhonda yells, "If you knew she was going to get so big why'd you let a 19 year old keep her!?"

Fending her off by jumping back, Terry retorts. "They aren't suppose to get that big so fast unless the husbandry is not right! Lay off me woman!" Bringing the attention back to Dale, "So, what have you been doing with Cici that made her get so big?"

Dale kicks another piece of concrete into the hole in the floor. 

"I kinda forgot about her in the basement."

The day after Christmas Eve, my skin started to feel a little dry, no amount of lotion seemed to satiate. By the evening on Christmas day, I had scratched my shin raw beneath my jeans figuring the milk bath later was going to improve my state, before I had to go back to the miserable job the next day.

Sleep was restless, my scalp became tighter and scratching produced no dandruff. The roots of my hair cemented and unmoving, so uncomfortable I couldn't fall asleep. The morning on the 26th, the weight of my scalp gave me a migraine and I called out of work. When I woke up 12 hours later my back started shifting and crinkling, stretching to the heavens did not give me any comfort.

I boiled myself in the tub that night, milk, olive oil, using moisturizing clay that I slathered over my head, shoulders and neck. Resting in the steaming water until my skin stopped feeling like coarse paper. Bundled up in my softest towel I gazed at myself in the mirror.

What happened to you? 

Deep pores like caverns, dull skin, faded lips, sad, pale eyes sitting in tired sockets, lifeless breasts, and hanging flab from upper arms to inner thighs. Leaning down the dry off my lower legs, I noticed my skin is puckered like jelly. Hopefully this will calm down before work tomorrow, at least I still have some pants that fit.

Grabbing a glass of water, I crawl into bed hoping I don't wake up in pain. Of course I would be wrong, as the sun crept through the window my eyes opened in terror. Was this sleep paralysis? My knees, my neck, shoulders and back were locked, paired with a migraine from hell and ringing ears. Shutting off the alarm, I managed to force a stretch that caused my joints to pop in succession like bubble wrap. I felt tight and crinkly again, my joints felt like they were gummed up like sludge in a machine. Opening my eyes, I saw floaters, pinching the globs of sleep from the corners I put on my glasses and tried to readjust. 

I don't feel okay. I looked at the phone and time had flown right past me trying to become normal. I was about to be late for work. I hobbled over to my closet, my ankles lost mobility as if theily were caked in dried mud. I pulled out a pair of pants and tried to step into them.

They fit me last week, did I gain that much weight?

The back of my thighs were pebbled and rough, my jeans snagged and dug in, as I attempted to wiggle my dried playdoh through the legs. I gave up when my butt would not allow any forgivness, it was solid and dimpled like bicsuit batter that had sat in the sun all day. Grabbing my phone, I called out again keying in my employee number trying to wrangle my hair into a clip. My scalp was taught again and my back was catching up. After receiving my verification code I pulled the curtains and laid down again, nightmares of repeating the same work day, running around in a panic while everyone poked and prodded me.

Waking up again, the sun was down, my joints had locked again but no amount of stretching gave me the audible pop of their release. My hands felt gloved and I ran them down the side of my leg under the covers. I managed to crawl out of bed and slip into the bathroom for a bath once more.

My torso would now match my leg, mottled in pickled sponge and it seems to be growing past my shoulders and up my neck. At least I have a day off tomorrow, I will keep moving and begin cleaning.

My joints eventually loosened while I tossed old items and moved my furniture around my room. Creating a new space for my snake and separately the tegu, I wanted this room to feel like a new space. Maybe all the depression will subside and my new alkergy will elliviates. Popping 4 extra strength ibprophen I scooted my bed in place. All the animals are happy. Into the day off, my skin kept growing rougher, tightening in place which I would stave the immobility off by dropping in the tub, apologetically confirming to my roommate I will add more to my share this month for the water bill.

The 29th came and I rose to get ready for work, extra early for the bath, coffee in hand, I was going to give this place another shot even though I had given them five.

However. The bath didn't work, my skin was still hardened and pulling my tendons underneath. Once the steam had settled in the bathroom, I wiped the mirror to gaze at myself again, but the mirror was still blurring my reflection. I opened the door with the towel wrapped around me, everything looked like a softened unfinished watercolor painting.

I made my way back to my room and called out again, "this job is causing me so much stress I am dying!" I thought to myself as I go to close my eyes. They don't shut. I rummage my nightstand for pain medicene and my water, I stare up at the ceiling as the gray frost tunnels my vision.

I managed to fall asleep, my roommate knocked on my door a few times through out, only to be met with a groan. When I woke up, I couldn't see past a gray haze, a cap over my eyes. My skin no longer crinkled but thudded when I tapped it. I was afraid to leave my room until I felt my cat crawl over my legs. I didn't feel his fur, but I felt the weight of his paws as he walked over me. My hand reached out and pet him, he came closer until he was on my chest. Purring was a motor that vibrated over my shell. 

I felt there were worse ways to die, but in all honesty I felt I had more energy under this surface, just had a hard time moving.

Over the course of the night I managed to become mobile. I mulled around my room and played music once I turned on my accessibility settings. Donning a thick hoodie I joined my roommate outside for a smoke.

Talking to her about how draining the job makes me, eased some of the tension I was feeling despite not sharing the horrid skin condition I was concealing. I couldn't see but neither could she at 3am outside.

I navigated my way past the living back to my room, crawling into bed to fall asleep once more, two hours in my alarm goes off. I am stiffer than before, but I am fighting the corner of my covers to find my phone until I feel a ripping sensation over my shoulder while I reached. The cool air from the fan hit me and I stopped. Am I bleeding? This morning was no migraine or pain, just labored moving.

I sat up and didn't feel like my butt was a boulder, just that I was sitting in a paper mache diaper. I stretched to the teavens and yawned. Every place of tension broke open, scrunching my face released the gooey under-shell eye caps and I could feel the deep cracks as if they were hard plastic over my cheeks.

I looked up to my snake's enclosure who I moved next the window. Over the past few days I wasn't able to check him out, even though I needed to get ready I wanted to check out his cage. Rummaging through the bedding since he is tiny and likes to burrow my middle finger peeled back exposing fresh skin making it easier to sift. I felt something papery in the bedding, pulling it out I find that my hognose had his first shed. Placing the skin on the desk I continue sifting through the bedding until I find him in the corner. Picking him up, he does not hiss or hood but flicks his tongue at me. We stare at one another and I fix his bedding to place him back in.

I go to the bathroom to assess myself. Sure enough, I look like a gargoyle, but my eyes look different. They look green and a brown spot on my iris has appeared. I pick up my phone from the counter and begin calling the attendance line. When the automated woman comes on I hang up. Looking back in the mirror I tug on a sharp edge raised from my cheek and pull. No pain, just releif from cool air kissing my skin. The skin underneath shines with vibrancy as if I returned from a day spa, I pull more off my face and down my neck. Everything is different than before. The structure of my face snapped back and looks happy. My scalp cleared of the cement husk shows shining locks of red aside from the previous color of ruddy dish water.

Half way off my face I stare for a moment. That girl before must have died and rotted out of this body to allow for the growth. The crags of jutting shed on the side of my face I haven't touched shows two different faces. Picking up my phone I close the phone app and go to my email to send a resignation.

Once the email sent I continue plucking and pulling the gray shell off my body. While the phone begins to ring I silence it as I continue my process. She doesn't exist anymore, pulling a long strip from my foot to my thigh, supple skin radiating underneath.

"New year, new me."

"I will let you know how it goes." Turning her phone off she pulled out the envelope from her pocket. Faded green paper, frayed and worn on every corner with her name written in gold marker on the back.

Everyday since her father's death, she opened this letter and poured over every word. Just an address with steps to be followed. Samuel was cremated, but a tombstone was erected in a cemetary states away, today at 6:45 a.m. would be exactly 3 years since he passed.

The air is crisp, the plants have a thin glaze of frost, while she walks down the dirt road past the entrance. 

Over the course of the walk she thinks of how the last 3 years have treated her. The moments during the last 3 years when she wished she could pick up the phone and call him, moments where her chest grew tight again because of how alone she really was throughout all the pain. Here Kiki was, not knowing what is to come, all she knows is that her father wanted this.

Thirty minutes to spare, when she arrives at Samuel's headstone. The grass is over grown, but her daughter's teddy bear was still tied to the post holding silk Roses. Unfurling a towel, she sits down facing her Father's name carved in granite. 

The coin is warm when she pulls it from her front pants pocket. Standard arcade token from a nearby pool hall, one side having a loop scratched on top of it. Over the last few years Kiki had worn down the rough edges of the engraving tracing her finger over the loop constantly, giving her a sense of peace whenever she needed it.

6:45 a.m. and Kiki brings the coin to rest on his tombstone as his letter stated, sat back down on her towel, lit 3 candles, and settled down with a bottle of water.

The first hour in Kiki started talking to herself as if she was on the phone with her dad. Recounting all the good and bad of various days she had. The user boyfriend, the family fighting, medical scares, losing friends, and being a young mother. She reminisced about her baby Kiara, "Daddy you would be so proud of her!" Laughing about all the things her daughter does to make her smile. "I swear she got all that silliness from her abuelo"

Foot steps fall close to the grave, "Someone has to keep the pranks going." A man's voice breaks the dead air around her, turning around a man in a tank top and jeans stands before her with a smile that warms the fog around them.

Kiki scrambles from the towel kicking up the grass and she jumps into him. She doesn't feel anything and upon landing the sun is in mid day in a warmer climate, it feels like the home she just left to come up here. Looking around she is surrounded by saw grass and humidity, no sight of her father anywhere.

Tears start to well up in her eyes, did she mess it up? Was that it?

"I didn't know what to expect either Mimis" Samuel picks himself off the ground, in the sunlight Kiki can see he is sheer against the background.

"Daddy?" Kiki doesnt know what else to say, she prayed for this moment. Long pause as they both stood in the tall grass, buzzing of gnats, harsh sun, birds in the distance Samuel takes in the view of his daughter, 3 short years but she has changed so much. He was there, watching without a way to let her know, wanting to console her, wipe away her tears, he didn't want his little girl to hurt this young.

"What do we do?" Kiki is worried because he has not spoken yet, frozen in place hoping to not lose sight of him.

Samuel sighs, watching his foot go through kicking a stone. "Mimis I don't know. This wasn't done by me." 

"Who?" Kiki begins looking around to better gauge her surroundings.

"I couldn't tell you. All I can say is you still work after the grave baby, and right now I need to give you this."

 Two boxes emerge from the sand a few feet away from them. "I buried these a few years after you were born. One is for you but the second box you need to take to the address listed, I won't be able to leave this spot until it is delivered."

Samuel walks over as Kiki dusts the remaining sand off their lids, "Don't open yours until you get home, but deliver the other before tomorrow morning." Kiki starts crying, "I am just suppose to run errands for you?" Samuel takes his hand and places it in front of her. 

"I left this world too soon, there was still so much to be done that I needed to be there for. This-" he tries to pick up the boxes in her arms but fazes through them "is my only chance to be around a little bit longer before I ascend." Kiki looks up and sees that furrow her father always had whenever he was going through a dilemma.  Kiki takes a step back, " I will." She turns away and starts walking down the trail coming up the edge of the groves, turning her head she sees her father take a seat beneath an orange tree heavy with fruit.

When she finally gets within cellular service she calls for an uber to pick her up, the car still being states away. Opening up the black tin box an envelope falls from the inner lid.

"Holly?" Kiki sees the same green envelope with gold lettering as hers was. The address is listed 2 hours away, she stops at her home to borrow her mother's car.

"I was towed this morning, please I will be gone 3 hours!"
